Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
910 PM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Trend has been a little slower with the onset of rain Sunday
morning/afternoon.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Coastal low to bring increased rain chances on Sunday.

- 2) Cooler temperatures next week with precipitation arriving
  for the Thanksgiving holiday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Coastal low to bring increased rain chances on 
Sunday.

Latest guidance coupled with 00Z RAOB noting the dry air present
in the area likely slowing the onset of precipitation Sunday
morning/afternoon. Otherwise, previous discussion follows.

The current setup at the surface features high pressure
retreating into New England. To the south, an inverted trough 
remains along the southeastern U.S. coastline while a wavy 
frontal zone stretches across central Florida to the north of 
the Bahamas. Over the next 12 to 24 hours, the persistent ridge
pulls into the Canadian Maritimes. At the same time, the 
frontal system around Florida is slated to lift northward, 
generally paralleling the Atlantic coastline. How close the 
accompanying wave(s) of embedded low pressure track will 
dictate the level of local impacts to the region. The latest
trend is for several disorganized low centers to consolidate
into a more cohesive system a bit further out to sea.

Winds are gradually shifting to easterly/onshore as the 
inverted coastal trough approaches. Any rain chances look to 
hold off until late tonight, perhaps longer given dry low-level 
profiles to start.

Latest 12Z guidance has come into better agreement keeping the
steadiest rain east of the area. Will continue to forecast a 
broad 0.10 to 0.25 inches over the area (perhaps slightly less
in the Shenandoah Valley), perhaps accompanied by a few pockets
approaching 0.50 inches toward the Chesapeake Bay. With a more 
offshore track of the series of lows, the strength of north to 
northeasterly winds remains limited, as well. Outside of the 
rain chances, high temperatures will mainly be in the mid 50s to
mid 60s on Sunday.

The forecast looks dry for the start of the new work week as an
upstream cold front moves through early Monday. A downsloping 
northwesterly wind will still help raise temperatures well into 
the 60s. This also produces a favorable upslope flow to produce 
some light showers along/west of the Allegheny Front. East of
the mountains, waves of stratocumulus clouds are possible. Wind
gusts may persist at times into Monday night behind a secondary
cold front that ushers in much cooler air.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler temperatures next week with precipitation 
arriving for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Behind multiple cold fronts, temperatures on Tuesday cool and return 
to late-November normals throughout the week. High pressure builds 
over the Ohio River Valley giving our area a brief break in 
rainfall until Wednesday evening.

Models are in good agreement for an elongated trough to dig into the 
Mississippi River Valley Wednesday into Thursday. This sets up
another coastal low pressure system to trail up the Mid-Atlantic 
coastline by Thanksgiving. This far out, both deterministic and 
ensemble guidance show a wide range of potential solutions, so it's 
far too early to get into specific details. Most of the solutions 
differ in how far this system will pass off the coast. A closer 
track would increase precipitation amounts and lead to gustier 
winds. At higher elevations, mixed wintry precipitation remains a 
possibility Thanksgiving Day, especially across the Alleghenies.
If this were to occur, snowfall amounts remain modest with 
recent guidance trending rainier.

Unless a deeper closed low develops, this system advances into 
the Atlantic by Friday. High pressure developes in the wake of this 
system, bringing seasonable, dry conditions for Friday.

&&

.AVIATION /02Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
VFR conditions are likely to persist through early Sunday
morning, with a gradual lowering and thickening of clouds. 
An easterly onshore wind this evening will become north to
northeast tonight through Sunday. Any restrictions from 
approaching showers should hold until Sunday.

Most aviation models suggest ceilings right along the fringes of
MVFR and VFR (3,000 feet or so). So any sub-VFR conditions will
likely be intermittent and be guided by how much rainfall tracks
through (which has trended less). Winds on Sunday are expected 
to be out of the north to northeasterly direction, with the 
strongest gusts likely east of the local airspace. Any rain 
chances diminish late Sunday night, though some patchy fog may
form. A cold front yields improving conditions for Monday,
though with waves of VFR stratocu likely. This comes with 
prevailing northwesterlies that gust to around 15 to 20 knots 
during the afternoon and into the night.

VFR conditions are likely Tuesday, although northwest winds may 
remain a bit gusty. Clouds may increase Wednesday ahead of coastal 
low pressure, but rain and sub-VFR conditions likely hold off until 
Wednesday night.

&&

.MARINE...
Expect modestly increasing east to northeasterly winds into 
Sunday as a wavy frontal zone approaches from the coastal 
Carolinas. Given a more eastward track, the strongest winds may 
stay east of the Chesapeake Bay. Brief periods of gusts 15-20
knots are possible over the mid bay, but confidence in duration
is too low for an SCA at the moment. A cold front then tracks 
in from the west early Monday with northwesterlies in the wake. 
The real uptick does not take place until Monday evening/night 
which will likely warrant Small Craft Advisories.

Potentially weaker winds Tuesday with Small Craft Advisory 
conditions remaining a possibility in northerly flow. Winds 
further increase Wednesday becoming northeasterly overnight as 
coastal low pressure develops.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A much moister environment moves into the entire region on Sunday
as an area of low pressure lifts up the Carolina coast. Winds 
pick up intensity early next week behind a strong cold front. 
This brings in cooler weather but also another round of reduced 
daily humidities. Another coastal system may bring wet and windy 
conditions to the region by the middle of next week, which may 
include a chance for mountain snow. This looks to continue into 
the Thanksgiving holiday, but uncertainty is high at this time.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Relatively light winds through Monday may allow for tides to
elevate somewhat, resulting in action stages at vulnerable sites
like Annapolis particularly late Monday afternoon. Thereafter,
strong offshore flow will result in decreasing tides Monday
night into Tuesday.

Another coastal low pressure area will likely move up the East
Coast Wednesday into Thursday. Depending on the evolution and
track, tide levels may rise once again.
